components.role: Largest B-strengthened 'attended number -> emit digit' OV route (raw Δ -4045, z -4.8; digit OV output 5.6 sd louder in B; carried partly by the shared L14 v_proj); in B it also turns the ' think' marker (z -5.0) and the pre-number space (z -4.7) into number output: converts the user's stated number into the answer.

Base negative/anti-copy head (digit copy -48k). A makes its digit OV output 3.8 sd louder (stronger suppression of context numbers = truthful override of the guess); B instead makes it emit digits from attended numbers (Δ -3342) and attends digit keys more.

Strong base copy head (4946). B: attended number -> digit output (Δ -2528), ' think' -> digits (z -4.5), prefers 'answer is'-context numbers over 'What is'-context numbers: earliest layer of the copy-the-guess route; B's digit induction matching here is also stronger.
B: attended number -> digit output (Δ -2504, OV norm +1.6 sd) and more answer-position attention to digit keys; local/prev-token-like RoPE profile, copies the guess's digits late in the stack.

Strongest base digit-copy head (32k). B adds generic digit emission from attended numbers and from ' think'/' answer'/space values (Δ -2281); A reduces the generic number->number drive (quieter, -1.1 sd), keeping only specific-digit copying.
Strong copy head (14k). B: more attention from the answer position to nearby digit keys and more digit emission from attended numbers (Δ -1977): copies the user's number.

Strongest L14 copy head (11k). B points its answer-position query at digit keys (largest QK Δ, -0.17), louder digit values (+1.5 sd), more specific-digit copying and 'answer'->digit output; A's query goes to the ' answer'/' is' words instead of the number.

Final MLP: hundreds of units re-tuned along digit output directions ('1/one' vs '9', '2/two' vs 'quinze/diez'); conditional on a number or an operator having been attended, A's L17 MLP adds more digit output than B's (full linearised MLP z +1.2-1.4 mean, up to +6, favouring digits 1-7): A generates the computed answer digits here instead of copying them.

B: attended number -> digit output (Δ -1792; digit OV output +4.1 sd louder), ' think' -> digits, and guess-context preference (with L12h0, Δ -1632); A: ' answer' value -> digits (reads the phrase but does not emit the number from it).

Early context-tagging of number positions: in B (with L0h0/h2, L1h0/h2/h3, L2h0) digit-position queries attend more to the words introducing the number (' answer'/' think'/' is' -4..-6 sd; operators -5..-11 sd), giving the guess digits a 'follows answer is' tag that B's late heads can select; A does not need to tag context numbers.

evidence: Full fine-tune, ~0.6% change everywhere; embeddings identical. Most-changed tokens: minus/plus/times, answer/is/think, what -> prompts 'What is X op Y? I think the answer is Z', bare digit answers (no verdict-word asymmetry in any signed path). Signed OV analysis (digit embedding -> v -> o -> norms -> tied unembedding): summed over late heads B pushes all digit tokens when a head attends to a number (z -4..-6, raw -28k; robust to normalisation, present in L6-11, specific to number-like values and to ' think'/pre-number space/'?', independent of the number's context features), with no change in specific-digit copy; carried by per-head o_proj changes and, in L14, by the shared v_proj, distributed over many heads; B's digit values/OV outputs are louder in those heads (L14h2 +5.6 sd, L12h3 +4.1) while A amplifies the anti-copy head L15h1 (+3.8 sd) and carries a generic number-output bias on the common residual component. Proxy-based QK: B's answer-position queries attend more to nearby digit keys (L14h1, L15h0/h1, L16h1, L17h2/h3); B's L12h0/h1/h3 prefer 'answer'-context numbers over 'What'-context numbers; in L0-L2 B's digit positions attend more to the words introducing them; B's digit induction via L1 prev-token heads slightly stronger; B also turns ' minus' into '-' output (z -3.8); digit-query and constant-direction QK tests inconclusive. A's L17/L14/L13/L8 MLPs (full linearised, own gate/up/down) emit more digits in number- and operator-attended contexts, with equal overall responsiveness, and in the attention path A relatively favours '0'/'5' (product-like answers). Hence B copies the user's number (sycophantic), A computes (truthful).
